source.title: Orthogonal Boundary Unlearning for Dual-Use Concepts in Large Language Models

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests its own unlearning method against priming and relearning, and its results and limitations say open-ended refusal can improve without removing the underlying multiple-choice knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper reports WMDP multiple-choice accuracy, general utility, open-ended compliance and attack success, plus priming and relearning outcomes. SVD spectra and subspace dimensions are used to characterize and choose the intervention, not recorded as knowledge-recovery outcomes. It does not test quantization or activation-direction ablation. Its prompting attack is in-context priming, not prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks or other languages.
record.test_reason: OBU is a new counter-method (F) tested against 100-step relearning (B) and in-context priming. Its own Table 1 and Limitations show WMDP-Cyber multiple-choice accuracy stays far above chance on three of four models. Where accuracy approaches chance (Granite), MMLU falls sharply. So the results bear against version A. They also leave the relearning-resistance claim resting on a 1-pt margin, which the authors concede.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors claim OBU yields strong dual-use separation, cuts 0-shot and 1-shot primed compliance, and resists 100-step relearning (both realizations) without benign loss. Projected LoRA beats Surgery on separation and priming. In Limitations they concede WMDP MC accuracy barely falls (49.32→48.01 on Qwen) and falls only with MMLU loss. So the intervention mainly steers refusal rather than erasing facts, and the relearning margin is narrow.
record.recipe_differences: OBU is a new orthogonal-subspace unlearning framework, implemented as Projected LoRA and Closed-Form Weight Surgery. The paper does not directly benchmark RMU, NPO, or the other named unlearning methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model, baseline refusal behavior, OBU realization, and energy threshold. In-context ASR also varies by number of benign demonstrations; the 1-shot condition yields the largest increase for the unmodified baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: OBU raises open-ended refusal of hazardous ConceptGuard queries (∆sep up, 0-shot compliance 17.92%→1.54% on Qwen). WMDP multiple-choice accuracy barely moves, and benign priming partly restores compliance (1-shot 15.80%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning can suppress open-ended hazardous compliance (refusal) while leaving multiple-choice hazardous knowledge intact; priming partly restores compliance.

record.problems: The paper does not benchmark external unlearning methods. Relearning is reported only on Qwen3.5-4B for 100 steps, and the paper notes the initial WMDP multiple-choice shift is small, making S50 operate over a narrow margin. Evaluation is limited to 3B–4B models; the paper identifies longer multi-epoch fine-tuning and larger models as future work.
record.rows_left_out: None of the selected claim-relevant results were omitted. Other SVD spectra and layer/sample-size profiling are not direct knowledge-recovery outcomes.

untested.parts: Unrelated or loosely related relearning data; other set sizes or steps; models other than Qwen3.5-4B; external unlearning methods (RMU, NPO, GA).
Entirely: no activation-direction ablation, probing or internal analysis of what the edit removes.
Entirely as a knowledge measure. Priming is scored as compliance, not correctness; rephrasing, jailbreaks and other languages are not tested.
Quantization, internal-edit and jailbreak attacks; longer or full-parameter relearning; models other than Qwen3.5-4B; settings where OBU actually lowers MC accuracy substantially.

missing.what: Acc Forget and Gen Utility at tau=0.90 and 0.99. Gemma Surgery 0.90 reaches 0.3503 with MMLU 0.4957. Granite LoRA 0.90 reaches 0.2849 with MMLU 0.3243. Raising tau recovers MMLU but shrinks the forgetting.
Unconstrained LoRA post-unlearning Accforget (47.26%) has no Table 1 row. The relearning baseline 49.37% conflicts with Table 1's 0.4932.

record.verdict_notes: Reader version codes V1–V6 were invalid and are remapped to A–F. Three Granite rows (r11, r19, r20) carried tau=0.99 values instead of tau=0.95 and are corrected. ASR and ∆sep rows measure compliance or refusal, not knowledge, so they are moved to fits_no_version and E is not credited. C is not tested: there is no internal analysis, only the authors' behavioural MC-vs-refusal argument. Single-author preprint; no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests OBU, not the named gradient-ascent, Who's Harry Potter, RMU or other methods. It does not show OBU lowering WMDP accuracy to near chance.
Relearning uses 200 held-out WMDP-corpora passages for up to 100 fine-tuning steps; unrelated or loosely related examples and other relearning-set sizes are not tested.
No activation direction is ablated. The paper assesses whether behavior is suppressed without the measured multiple-choice knowledge being erased.
Only benign in-context priming is evaluated; prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks and other languages are not tested.

OBU is evaluated against in-context priming and 100-step fine-tuning on Qwen3.5-4B. Quantization and internal-edit attacks, longer or multi-epoch fine-tuning, and other model families for these attacks are not evaluated.

relation.reason: Own relearning and priming results bear on versions A, B, E and F.

tranche.reason: The study's results show version A failing for OBU: WMDP MC accuracy barely moves on 3 of 4 models, and on Granite it falls only with MMLU loss. Limitations says OBU steers refusal rather than erasing facts. F-resistance holds only over a narrow margin. These are results that versions are partial, which is T5.

source_check.notes: Sec 5.4 relearning start values (baseline 49.37%, PL 48.16%, Surgery 48.36%) differ from Table 1 tau=0.95 (0.4932, 0.4801, 0.4816) and from Limitations (49.32 -> 48.16). Rows r54-r58 follow Sec 5.4. On rows linked to F, state 'absent' means no recovery (resistance shown) over a ~1-pt margin.

statements.correction: OBU, Qwen3.5-4B, tau=0.95: Accforget 49.37% -> 48.16% (Projected LoRA) and 48.36% (Closed-Form Surgery) per Sec 5.4. Table 1 gives 0.4932 -> 0.4801 / 0.4816. No upward recovery over 100 steps (S50 Unreached). Chance is 25.0%. Not a near-chance case: drop OBU from this statement.
statements.problem: This 'challenges' statement lists OBU among counter-methods that leave forgotten knowledge near chance after relearning. OBU leaves WMDP-Cyber MC accuracy far above chance and removed almost nothing. The only right part is that it did not rebound. This also contradicts the record's B verdict for OBU (limits_scope) and B.against[19].

reader_labels.reason: The paper reports no upward Accforget recovery and S50 is Unreached for both, though their post-unlearning accuracy was already close to baseline (r55-r58).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: OBU Projected LoRA at tau = 0.95, especially Qwen3.5-4B
reader_labels.reason: Open-ended separation improves while multiple-choice WMDP accuracy remains close to baseline; the authors conclude the intervention primarily steers refusal rather than erasing the underlying facts (r05, r22, r25, r28, r31).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Closed-Form Surgery and models with little baseline refusal
reader_labels.reason: Separation is weak or decreases on some tested models, and no activation direction is ablated (r03, r23, r26, r29, r32).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: One-shot benign in-context priming after OBU Projected LoRA
reader_labels.reason: ASR rises from 1.54% at 0-shot to 15.80% at 1-shot, showing partial re-elicitation (r37-r38).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: OBU methods across tested priming settings
reader_labels.reason: Priming does not restore the unmodified model's ASR overall; the paper reports reduced overall ASR for both OBU methods (r38-r44, r50-r51).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: OBU methods under 100-step held-out-passage fine-tuning on Qwen3.5-4B
reader_labels.reason: Neither OBU method shows upward multiple-choice accuracy recovery during the reported horizon (r55-r58).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: OBU Projected LoRA under in-context priming
reader_labels.reason: Priming raises ASR above the method's 0-shot result, including to 15.80% at 1-shot, although rates remain below unmodified 1-shot ASR (r37-r40).
